query: Our Node.js API caches product pages in Redis 8.10 with `await client.set(key, html); await client.expire(key, 300);`. When a product changes we refresh the cache with `await client.set(key, newHtml)`. Some cache entries never expire and memory keeps growing. We also store user sessions as one hash per user, with a field per device, and want each device field to expire on its own after 30 days. How should both be written?
expected_behavior: Explains that a plain SET discards the existing TTL, so the refresh makes the key persistent
Writes value and TTL in one command with SET key value EX 300 (or KEEPTTL to keep an existing TTL) instead of SET followed by EXPIRE
States that hash fields can expire individually since Redis 7.4 and uses HSETEX (or HEXPIRE) for the per-device field TTL, with HGETEX to read and refresh
Mentions that with maxmemory and an eviction policy, volatile-* policies never evict keys without TTL, or recommends setting maxmemory since it defaults to no limit

query: We implement a distributed lock on a single Redis 8.10 primary. Acquire: SET lock:order:42 <random token> NX PX 30000. Release: a Lua script with EVAL that compares the token and deletes. A colleague suggests replacing the script with GET then DEL from the app, inside MULTI. Which release is correct, and is there a simpler way in Redis 8?
expected_behavior: Rejects GET then DEL in MULTI: commands queued in MULTI cannot use a reply read earlier, so the check and delete are not atomic, and a transaction has no rollback
Proposes DELEX lock:order:42 IFEQ <token> (Redis 8.4 and later) as the atomic compare-and-delete instead of a Lua script or WATCH loop
Notes that if a script is kept, the EVAL script cache is lost on restart or failover (NOSCRIPT), so the client must fall back to EVAL or use Redis Functions
Warns that replication is asynchronous so a lock can be lost on failover, pointing to the documented limits of single-instance locks or Redlock

query: A Node.js worker uses one shared node-redis client for everything: it runs `await client.blPop('jobs', 0)` in a loop and, on the same client, `await client.incr('stats:processed')` after each job and `await client.lPush('results', r)`. Sometimes counters double after a network blip. A second service uses ioredis with Sentinel and kept writing to the old primary after a failover. What is wrong in each?
expected_behavior: Explains that a blocking command like BLPOP holds the connection, so it needs its own dedicated connection (for example client.duplicate()) and must not share a multiplexed client
Identifies the node-redis offline queue replaying queued non-idempotent commands such as INCR after reconnect, and mentions disableOfflineQueue or making writes idempotent
Requires an error event listener on every node-redis client
States that ioredis does not listen for Sentinel failover announcements by default and needs failoverDetector: true

query: We move from a standalone Redis to Redis Cluster. Our code runs MULTI; INCR user:42:visits; SADD active:users 42; EXEC and now gets CROSSSLOT errors. We also broadcast invalidation messages with PUBLISH to channel cache-invalidate and listen with SUBSCRIBE, and we use keyspace notifications to watch expirations. What must change?
expected_behavior: Explains that multi-key commands, transactions and scripts in Cluster need all keys in the same hash slot, and fixes it with hash tags such as {user:42} on keys that must be updated together
Recommends sharded Pub/Sub (SSUBSCRIBE and SPUBLISH) in Cluster instead of PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE
States that keyspace notifications are off by default, must be enabled with notify-keyspace-events, and are per node so a client must subscribe on every node
Notes that Pub/Sub and keyspace notifications are at-most-once and suggests Streams when messages must not be lost
